chapter: New York bands and the first records
title: Forming the band for Bar Harbor
summary: A Commodore Record Shop employee forms Rudy Vallee's New Yorkers for Bar Harbor; Norvo recruits Eddie Sauter, Dave Barbour, Herbie Haymer and others.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well that was a little later and so then Commodore Record shop, a guy who worked there, formed a band called the Rudy Vallee's New Yorker's.
And we were supposed to go to Bar Harbor Maine, and work.
-- and I thought this is great. This is what I want.
So I got all the guys that I knew, had beenwith Charlie, they weren't working that summer --
-- Toots Commarata and Eddie Sauter were the three trumpets --
-- Bill Miler, two pianos, Bob Lane -- remember Bob Lane who was at -- piano -- Swedish fella that was in town?
No, I don't think I do remember him.
A wonderful band. I got a lot of arrangements, I got some from Teddy Hill who I knew -- he let me have some --
We copied them and give them back to him. Charlie had a few, we had some nice charts. So we went up there and I swear the people in Bar Harbor no idea what we were doing. No idea what we were doing.
